blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Customs is the government office at every border. It checks what is coming in and going out. Every shipment must be declared. The declaration tells customs what is in the box, how much it is worth, and where it came from. Taxes are calculated from that information.

Compliance means following the rules. Not just customs rules, but product rules, packaging rules, labelling rules, and safety rules. Different countries have different requirements, and they change often.

For a logistics team, compliance is boring on a good day and very expensive on a bad one.

items.q: What does customs check at the border?
options: What is coming in and going out
How many workers a company has
items.why: "It checks what is coming in and going out."

items.q: What does the declaration tell customs?
options: Only the weight of the box
What is in the box, its value, and where it came from
items.why: "The declaration tells customs what is in the box, how much it is worth, and where it came from."

items.q: How are taxes calculated?
options: From the information in the declaration
From the size of the truck
From the day of the week
From the number of boxes only
items.why: "Taxes are calculated from that information."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Rules can change from country to country
Compliance is easy and never a problem
A declaration is needed for every shipment
Customs checks goods at the border
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que compliance pode ser "very expensive on a bad one" — não é sempre fácil.

items.q: "Compliance is boring on a good day and very expensive on a bad one" suggests that…
options: a mistake in compliance can cost a lot of money
items.why: Inferência: um "bad day" (erro) fica caro — por isso as regras importam.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte treinando o novo assistente de compliance. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome to the team. Today I want to show you the questions that always come up when customs stops a shipment. Do not worry — they are the same questions every time.

First, customs asks: what is in the box? You must give a clear answer. Second, they ask: how much is it worth? The value is on the declaration. Third, where does it come from? The country of origin changes the tax.

Here is one rule you must remember. We keep every record for five years. If customs calls next year, we need the paper. No paper, big problem.

And listen — one small labelling mistake can stop a shipment at the border for days. So we check the label twice. Always twice. I know it is boring, but a bad day at customs costs the company a lot of money. Reading the rules is part of the job. Any questions? Good. Let's start with the first shipment.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the FIRST question customs asks?
items.why: "First, customs asks: what is in the box?"

items.q: How long does the team keep every record?
items.why: "We keep every record for five years."

items.q: What can one small labelling mistake do?
options: Stop a shipment at the border for days
items.why: "one small labelling mistake can stop a shipment at the border for days."

items.q: Why does Charlotte say "No paper, big problem"?
options: Because without the record they cannot answer customs
items.why: Inferência: se customs ligar e não houver registro, o time fica sem prova — daí o problema.

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's advice?
items.why: Inferência: ela repete "always twice" e explica cada passo — é cuidadosa e prática.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The box was stopped at customs for one day." Customs is…
options: the government office at the border
items.why: Customs = alfândega, o escritório do governo na fronteira.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Every shipment must have a ___ that says what is inside."
items.why: Declaration = declaração, o documento que diz o que há na caixa.

items.q: "We must declare the goods." To declare means to…
options: tell customs what the goods are
items.why: To declare = declarar, informar à alfândega o conteúdo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Wrong ___ on the box can stop the shipment. Always check the label."
items.why: Labelling = rotulagem; um erro no rótulo trava o envio.

items.q: "Following the rules is called compliance." Compliance means…
items.why: Compliance = conformidade, seguir as regras.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem no trabalho de logística e compliance. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager must sign off on the declaration before we send it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new labelling rule next month." To roll out means to…
options: start using it step by step
items.why: Roll out = implementar aos poucos.

items.q: "Please fill out the customs form before lunch." To fill out means to…
items.why: Fill out = preencher o formulário.

items.q: "We agreed to check the labels, but the team never followed through." They…
options: did the job to the end
did not finish what they agreed
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim; aqui, não levaram.

items.q: "Customs held up the shipment for two days." To hold up means to…
items.why: Hold up = atrasar, segurar algo.
